finding: A module-level edit costs the same wherever it lands: editing the leaf Emit.v, which nothing depends on, costs 115.9s against a 129.8s cold prover build, and editing Float.v at the head of the critical path costs 116.2s. The Rocq theory itself is 15.0s of critical path over 16 modules, so the saving the dependency graph implies is not being realised. Cache is not the remedy: any code change invalidates it, and going forward every change is a code change.
observed_cost: 115.9s leaf vs 116.2s foundation vs 129.8s cold; Rocq critical path 15.0s

finding: Two policy gates are 92% of every commit. precommit.mutation is 71.5s and precommit.naming 27.3s of a 107.2s warm hook, while the complete proof gate is 1.6s and the whole-tree go build 1.7s. At the top level make.check is 245.5s cold and 245.8s warm, so caching buys nothing, whereas make.prove goes 129.8s cold to 1.6s warm. The Docker layers cache; the host-side Python does not.

The mutation harness copies the whole repository per mutant, and .build-observatory (50 MB over the run bundles) is absent from its ignore patterns, so roughly 90% of each copy is the observatory own raw logs. In the pre-commit path the hook has already exported the tree, so it makes 103 copies to test 102 one-line substitutions, and each mutant then re-runs the FULL self-test when only its 1-3 named controls depend on the rule. Rob directs using git as the incremental modification tool — temporary commits and reset to switch states — rather than copying, and notes copying is probably not worth it for parallelism either. Also a hygiene defect: every fixture tree currently contains stale observation bundles, so tree-walking gates are tested against polluted input.
observed_cost: 71.5s of a 107.2s hook; ~55 MB copied per mutant

finding: build_targets restates a fact the Makefile already owns: ten --target clauses hand-copied into ten registry entries. TENSION, not a settled finding — it passes review completely, being declared, validated against the Dockerfile graph, controlled and mutation-covered, and fails only the one-authority-per-fact rule. Candidate reconciliation, offered unranked and not recommended: derive it from the Makefile recipes at load and keep validating the derivation against the stage graph, which leaves the Makefile the only authority and loses no verification. Whether a well-tested duplication is acceptable here is a judgement for Rob and the reviewer, not something this ledger should settle.
evidence_ids: no metric — a structural finding, not a timing one
